en: Homage to Vajraḍāka!
Since an extensive [explanation] would generally be difficult for children and women to grasp, one should extract that seven-syllable [mantra], having condensed even what was already concise. (1)
Between the beginning with worship and the end with the realization of emptiness and the mantra,
one should accomplish Vajraḍāka by means of the primary and secondary limbs.
One should visualize [the syllables] Yaṃ, Raṃ, Vaṃ, and Laṃ upon the maṇḍalas of the four elements.
[Visualize] Mount Meru, born from the syllable *suṃ*, possessing eight peaks made of the seven precious gems.
*Oṃ medini vajrībhava vajrabandha hūṃ*. *Oṃ vajraprākāra hūṃ vaṃ hūṃ*.
Oṃ vajrapañjara hūṃ paṃ hūṃ | Oṃ vajravitāna hūṃ khaṃ hūṃ | Oṃ vajraśarajāla trāṃ śaṃ trāṃ |
Oṃ vajrajvālānalārka hūṃ hūṃ hūṃ!
Having fashioned the sixfold foundation beginning with the vajra-ground, one should draw a six-spoked wheel situated upon a universal lotus and encircled by a garland of universal vajras. 4.
One should meditate right here on Hūṃbhava as Vajraḍāka, the Great Bliss— one with six arms, three faces, and three eyes, endowed with all the [major] marks (lakṣaṇa),
joined with the eighty minor characteristics (vyañjana), and the Lord arisen from Āli and Kāli.
He is absorbed in union with the Vajra-bell, wearing human skin over his upper body;
in his left hands he holds a skull-cup and a *khaṭvāṅga*, and in his right hand a trident;
he wears a crown of skulls, and his matted hair is adorned with a double-vajra (*viśvavajra*).
He has the crescent moon as his crest-ornament, and his body is adorned with the six mudrās;
his faces are blue, yellow, and green, and he is clothed in a tiger-skin garment.
He stands in the ālīḍha posture, treading upon Bhairava and Kālarātri who are situated upon the sun.

As it is for the Lord, so too for Vajravārāhī, with her arms and so forth. (9) Enveloping the knees of the Goddess, overwhelmed by supreme bliss, she should perform the summoning of gnosis and the other rites with these syllables: JAḤ HŪṂ VAṂ HOḤ. (10)
The six yoginīs are situated upon the six spokes by revolving in a counter-clockwise direction:
the first goddess is Herukī, the second is Vajrabhairavī,
the third is Ghoracaṇḍī, and the fourth is Vajrabhāskarī.
The fifth is Vajra-raudrī, and the sixth should be Vajra-ḍākinī.
These goddesses are blue, yellow, red, green, smoke-colored, and white;
they have disheveled hair, are extremely fierce, possess three eyes, and are naked.
Holding battle-drums and bells in their two hands other than the one [holding the skull-cup],
wearing human skins, and standing upon a corpse and the sun,
they wear crowns of garlands of skulls and are established in the ālīḍha posture.

All the auspicious goddesses born from the six syllables are established in their respective order by these five elements: *lāṃ*, *māṃ*, *pāṃ*, *tāṃ*, and *khaṃ*. One should purify the aggregates (*skandhas*), such as form and the rest, with the syllables *oṃ*, *aṃ*, *hrīṃ*, *hūṃ*, *hoḥ*, and *hrīḥ*. One should purify the sense bases (*āyatanas*) with the syllables *bhrūṃ*, *hūṃ*, *khaṃ*, *āḥ*, *ho*, and *haṃ*. One should apply [the following] to the chest, head, shoulders, eyes, and so forth: *oṃ haḥ*, *namaḥ hiḥ*, *svāhā hūṃ*, *vauṣaṭ he*, *hūṃ hūṃ hoḥ*, *phaṭ phaṭ*. [And likewise: *oṃ vaṃ*, *hāṃ yoṃ*, *hriṃ moṃ*, *hreṃ hrīṃ*, *hūṃ hūṃ*, *phaṭ phaṭ*.
One should perform the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) at the navel, heart, mouth, head, crest-lock, and elsewhere; one should project the syllables *oṃ*, *āḥ*, and *hūṃ* into the body, speech, and mind.

One should consecrate [the practitioner] with skull-cups filled with the liquid of the five nectars, held in the hands of the hosts of goddesses residing within the wheel of the six-chakra sovereign. 16
Having performed worship, praise, and the tasting of nectar, one should practice meditative cultivation;
the mantra-practitioner should recite the seven-syllable mantra with a mind free from doubt:
*oṃ hrīḥ ha ha hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ*.

When one becomes weary from meditation and recitation, then one should contemplate purity. Śrī Heruka is the factor of enlightenment that is mindfulness (*smṛti-saṃbodhyaṅga*); Herukī is the factor of enlightenment that is the investigation of phenomena (*dharmapravicaya-saṃbodhyaṅga*); Vajrabhairavī is the factor of enlightenment that is vigor (*vīrya-saṃbodhyaṅga*); Ghoracaṇḍī is the factor of enlightenment that is joy (*prīti-saṃbodhyaṅga*); Vajrabhāskarī is the factor of enlightenment that is pliancy (*prasrabdhi-saṃbodhyaṅga*); Vajra-raudrī is the factor of enlightenment that is concentration (*samādhi-saṃbodhyaṅga*); and Vajraḍākinī is the factor of enlightenment that is equanimity (*upekṣā-saṃbodhyaṅga*). This is the cultivation of the seven factors of enlightenment. [The ornaments are: the necklace, the bracelet, the jewel, the earring, the ashes, and the sacred thread.
Indeed, these six perfections are joined together in the form of mudrās. || 19 ||
The seven-syllable sādhana extracted by Durjayacandra is completed.
